clue.text: Arts of astronomy

parts.note: the word arts is the four letters of a twinkling body in the sky put into a changed order, so it is that word made variable

explanation.surface: A heading in a syllabus listing the arts subjects belonging to astronomy.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as instructions, VARIABLE (shuffle) applied to STAR, and you get ARTS. 'of astronomy' then marks the answer as a term from that science.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable star is a term from the science of the heavens: a star whose brightness changes over time.

clue.text: One can put tax on residence in Rome

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tax is levied on a home in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... on' sets the British value added tax ahead of the other pieces; in Rome the residence is the papal one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the papal palace and seat of the pope, within Rome.

clue.text: Computer production to study (not at home)

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
out means away from home

explanation.surface: A programmer studies while away from the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A readout is the information a computer displays or prints.

clue.text: "The great Made my mate' (Stevenson)

parts.note: a gap-fill from Stevenson's poem 'My Wife': 'The great ___ / Made my mate', naming the divine craftsman

explanation.surface: A line of Stevenson's poetry with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is in Stevenson's Songs of Travel; the blank names a skilled maker, here God.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman or inventor, here the Creator who fashioned the poet's wife.

clue.text: Bar for uplift at opening time

definitions.text: Bar for uplift at opening time

parts.words: Bar for uplift at opening time
parts.note: not a pub at opening time but a door fastening, a bar you raise when you open the door

explanation.surface: A pub where drinkers go for a lift when the doors open.
explanation.definitionFit: A door fastening of a bar that falls into a catch, lifted to open the door.

clue.text: Object making stink up in space?

indicators.note: in space suggests the letters drifting apart and coming together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rocket launch that leaves a smell in orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: STINK UP rearranged gives the Soviet satellite of 1957, the first object put in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite, a man-made body sent into orbit.

clue.text: He decides to barter with one perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the trading word plus a numeral could be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dealer chooses whether to trade with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BARTER and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or referee settles disputes, so is a person who decides.

clue.text: Trilby employed as small-scale demonstrator

parts.note: employed means in work
Trilby, heroine of George du Maurier's novel, was an artist's model

explanation.surface: A felt hat put to use as a miniature demonstration piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trilby' looks like the hat, but the hat was named after du Maurier's heroine, who sat for painters in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaled-down replica that actually runs, used to show how a machine works.

clue.text: Ishmael's clue for "cats"

parts.note: the four letters of this word, cast out of their order, give a word for a mould or a troupe of actors

explanation.surface: A crossword setter called Ishmael offers a clue whose answer is cats.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: take the answer as instructions, CAST put OUT of order, and the letters make CATS. Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar, was driven into the desert in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael is the biblical type of the rejected exile, sent away with his mother Hagar.

clue.text: Begged aid going places

parts.note: asking for help with travel by raising a digit at the roadside, as a hitchhiker does

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded for help while out and about.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitchhiker signals for a lift with a raised hand, asking drivers for help on the road.

clue.text: Not the motivation for a mule-train though

definitions.text: Not the motivation for a mule-train though

parts.words: Not the motivation for a mule-train though
parts.note: the name sounds like animal power, but it is a small auxiliary steam engine, not the beasts pulling a mule-train

explanation.surface: A remark about what does not pull a train of pack animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey engine is a small auxiliary steam engine, used on ships for winches and pumps.

clue.text: No thrill at start of game

parts.note: a kick is a buzz of excitement
off means not on, cancelled, as in 'the deal is off'

explanation.surface: A dull opening to a match that offers no excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse of the clue's order: thrill first, then the word for 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the match begins with the ball being booted from the centre spot.

clue.text: In Devon this place has twenty per cent off for its product

definitions.text: In Devon this place has twenty per cent off for its product

parts.words: In Devon this place has twenty per cent off for its product
parts.note: a Devon town famed for the fine lace made there; the twenty per cent seems to play on lace being reduced or cut away, a riddle about the town's craft

explanation.surface: A Devon town runs a twenty per cent sale on the goods it is known for.
explanation.walkthrough: The town in east Devon gave its name to a delicate bobbin lace. The 'twenty per cent off' joke is not fully explained by any letter play found.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Devon market town is known worldwide for its handmade bobbin lace.

clue.text: Sort of saw return of this music group

indicators.note: return asks for the saw's name to be read from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: a tenon saw is a short stiff-backed saw used by joiners

explanation.surface: A musical ensemble keeps returning to some old proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a proverb but is the carpenter's tool; TENON turned round gives NONET.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine players, or a piece written for nine.

clue.text: A check that is right perhaps, for red squirrel

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters gathered might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written
ie is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether ticking a box beside a red squirrel is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles A, CHECK, IE and R into the North American squirrel's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickaree is the small reddish squirrel of North American conifer forests.

clue.text: Morpheus's unsuccessful lover

parts.note: Morpheus is the god of dreams; one who longs for his embrace but never gets it cannot fall asleep

explanation.surface: A tale of someone spurned by the Greek god of dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the arms of Morpheus' means asleep, so a failed suitor of Morpheus lies awake.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who habitually cannot sleep never reaches the arms of the dream god.

clue.text: Island chap, a sailor, writing to an old soldier

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, and a man is a chap
tar is an old word for a seaman
MS is manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A Manxman who is a sailor writes a letter to a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' simply joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-at-arms was a medieval soldier, especially a heavily armed mounted one.

clue.text: No "bird over a pound trifling

parts.note: taken as written
the mina, or myna, is an Asian starling that mimics speech
L is from libra, the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Refusing a bird that costs more than a pound is a minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets the pieces above one another in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal sum is a token one, very small and of little consequence.

clue.text: Swear, if touchy about it

indicators.note: about means the irritable word goes round the small conditional word

parts.note: testy means irritable, easily annoyed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cursing if someone is irritable about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the irritable word go round the conditional; the word 'it' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to declare under oath, as a witness does in court.

clue.text: Period useful for getting: around

definitions.meaning: a bicycle, handy for travelling about town

explanation.surface: A stretch of time handy for getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is both a recurring span of time and, short for bicycle, a means of transport.

clue.text: Pirate's vulgar-sounding accompaniment to song

indicators.note: sounding says the word for crude is used only for how it is said

parts.note: coarse means crude or vulgar
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A buccaneer's rude singing to go with his shanty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompaniment to' joins the sound of COARSE with AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer of the Barbary coast, a sea raider.

clue.text: Men like Shaw, all ready made, said Byron

definitions.text: Men like Shaw, all ready made, said Byron

parts.words: Men like Shaw, all ready made, said Byron
parts.note: Shaw wrote reviews of music and plays; Byron's satire English Bards and Scotch Reviewers says reviewers need no apprenticeship

explanation.surface: Byron's verdict on writers like George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Byron: 'A man must serve his time to every trade / Save censure — critics all are ready made.'
explanation.definitionFit: Reviewers who judge plays and music, as Shaw did for London papers, are the class Byron mocked.

clue.text: Some said a Moselle wine give it a miss

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice to skip the German wine others have recommended.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'wine give it a miss' as definition, but the answer is an old word for a young woman: 'miss' alone defines it, and 'wine give it a' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Damosel is an archaic form of damsel, a young unmarried woman, a maiden.

clue.text: Stone fruit, this berry?

definitions.meaning: a ... stone is a rocking stone, a balanced boulder found in Cornwall
add berry and you have the raspberry cross named after Judge ...

explanation.surface: A question about a stone fruit and a berry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone fruit' looks like plum or cherry, but the two words belong to separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish rocking boulder is a logan stone, and the loganberry is a hybrid bramble fruit.

clue.text: Omar's early stone-thrower

parts.note: in FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, dawn flings a stone into the bowl of night to put the stars to flight

explanation.surface: A Persian poet tells of a stone thrown at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening of the Rubaiyat: 'Awake! for Morning in the Bowl of Night / Has flung the Stone that puts the Stars to Flight'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the dawn is the one that hurls the stone, so the early part of the day is the thrower.

clue.text: Space found at the end of some flights

definitions.text: Space found at the end of some flights

parts.words: Space found at the end of some flights
parts.note: flights of stairs end on a level platform, and air flights end on touching down

explanation.surface: Room to spare when a plane journey is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The level area at the top of a staircase shares its name with an aircraft touching down.

clue.text: Story of Hamlet's play written in this tongue.

definitions.text: Story of Hamlet's play written in this tongue

parts.words: Story of Hamlet's play written in this tongue
parts.note: Hamlet says of the play within the play that the story is extant and written in very choice language of a southern European country

explanation.surface: A question about which language the Prince of Denmark's play was originally written in.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet III.ii: 'The story is extant, and written in very choice Italian.'
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet describes the source tale of his Mousetrap play as written in the language of Venice and Rome.

clue.text: Activity with the pack?

parts.note: the pack is a deck, not a pack of hounds or a rucksack, and the activity is a game of whist or bridge

explanation.surface: A hunting or scouting pastime with the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of bridge or poker is an activity done with a deck of fifty-two.
